about: Production-build size budget per emitted chunk, in bytes of gzip level 9 output. Each chunk is judged by the first rule whose pattern matches its file name; a chunk no rule matches fails the check. Lowering a limit is free. Any other change to a rule (a raised limit or Stage 2 target, a new, removed, rematched or reordered rule) needs a new changelog entry naming that rule. See scripts/bundle-budget.mjs.

changelog.change: Stage 1 of #971, set once #968 made the release build the minified one. Measured at 101d0904: entry 243,072, dialog host 191,285, heatmap-3d 159,867 bytes gzip.

Stage 2 of #971, activated by #969. Every dialog is now its own lazy chunk, so the catch-all drops from 200,000 to its Stage 2 target of 60,000, and both Stage 2 targets are retired as met (three's already equalled its limit). No dialog needs a rule of its own. The irrigation dialog was expected to, but it is the largest at 45,626 bytes gzip. Measured on 8f1b4002 plus #969: irrigation-dialog 45,626, strain-library-dialog 39,706, label-templates 37,841, config-dialog 37,552, dialog host 9,231 bytes gzip.

#970 lowers the measured production entry from 244,100 to 193,300 bytes gzip after removing luxon, moving TC/label probes and optional graphs behind lazy chunks. The 170,000-byte target remains out of reach without a larger change to eagerly used chart/header code or the Zod classic schema style: Zod classic itself imports JSON-schema conversion and its mini flavor has a different schema API. Set the enforceable entry limit to 195,000 bytes from this build, and retire the unmet Stage 2 target.

#974 raises the entry from 195,000 to 200,000 bytes gzip for the irrigation safety chip, its detail and the Emergency Stop. Measured at 1b715d3c plus #974: entry 198,767 bytes gzip, 4.3 KB over dev, of which the chip and its detail are 2.1 KB and the safety slice, its localized labels and the tank card's hold note the rest. It stays in the entry on purpose: the lazy dialog chunks are what a stale HACS install loses first (ADR 0053), and an emergency stop that 404s with them is not one. A chip-only entry with a lazy detail would still exceed the 500 bytes of headroom 195,000 left.

GSM#668 raises the entry from 200,000 to 205,000 bytes gzip for the Active Grow Run chip in the header, its Start dialog, the grow-run slice and its localized labels. Measured at dev df785598: entry 199,162 bytes gzip; with the run chip 201,300, 2,138 bytes over dev and 1,300 over the old limit. The chip is part of the header the entry already renders, beside the safety chip. The remaining 3.7 KB is headroom for the rest of the Grow Run MVP's header surface (#669, #671); the Grow Run View itself (#675) belongs in a lazy chunk.
